t: The Latin Empire was created after the crusaders captured and plundered Constantinople in April 1204, with a Catholic emperor enthroned in place of the Orthodox Roman emperors.
Venice received three eighths of the empire in the Partitio terrarum imperii Romaniae, and its podestà in Constantinople was practically independent of the emperor.
Constant war with Bulgaria and the Byzantine successor states wore the empire down until a Nicaean force of 800 soldiers took Constantinople in July 1261.
dyk: To raise money, Baldwin II stripped the lead roofs of the Great Palace and sold them, handed his only son Philip to Venetian merchants as a guarantee for a loan, and sold the relic of the Crown of Thorns.
ev: The crusaders capture and plunder Constantinople, elect Baldwin I emperor on 9 May and crown him in the Hagia Sophia on 16 May
At the Battle of Adrianople the Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan crushes the Latin knights and captures Emperor Baldwin
The Treaty of Nymphaeum recognises Latin control of most of Bithynia and Mysia
The Latin army is defeated at the battle of Poimanenon, and Thessalonica falls to Epirus
The last Latin possessions in Asia fall to Nicaea, and a joint Nicaean and Bulgarian siege of Constantinople fails
Michael VIII Palaiologos of Nicaea wins the Battle of Pelagonia
On the night of 24/25 July Alexios Strategopoulos enters Constantinople and restores the Byzantine Empire

f.founder: The leaders of the Fourth Crusade; Baldwin I (Baldwin IX of Flanders) was its first emperor
f.successor: Byzantine Empire, restored by the Empire of Nicaea under Michael VIII Palaiologos
